title: Add sales demo app with scripted scenarios (chat + structured output + tool calling)
author: Renee Sullivan
description:
## Context
We need a reliable, repeatable live-demo artifact that SEs can run (and re-run) in the demo tenant without hand-editing prompts or copy/pasting curl commands. This PR adds a small "Sales Demo App" that showcases: (1) chat completions w/ streaming, (2) structured output (JSON schema) and validation, (3) tool calling, and (4) retry + basic failure-mode handling so we can keep a demo moving.

This is intended to back the "Core API demo" scenario in the demo tenant: a single command runs the same scripted flow, and we can show the expected outputs in the UI/terminal to make regressions obvious.

## What’s included
- New demo app under `apps/sales-demo/` (TypeScript + Node) with a minimal web UI and a CLI scenario runner.
- Scenario runner (`pnpm demo:run --scenario <name>`) that executes a deterministic sequence:
  - Streaming chat completion (token streaming to terminal + optional SSE to UI)
  - Tool call: `lookup_order_status(order_id)` (local stub, deterministic)
  - Tool call: `get_weather(city)` (local stub, deterministic)
  - Structured output: returns a JSON object conforming to a provided schema (validated at runtime)
- "Golden" expected outputs captured per scenario (stable snapshots) + a `--update-goldens` mode for controlled refresh.
- Small set of scenarios mapped to the standard talk track:
  - `01-core-chat-streaming`
  - `02-tool-calling-order-lookup`
  - `03-structured-output-triage-json`
  - `04-retries-and-timeouts` (simulates transient 5xx + reconnect; does not rely on real outages)
- Configuration for demo stability:
  - Supports pinning `REDWOOD_DEMO_MODEL` and `REDWOOD_DEMO_MODEL_VERSION` (defaults align with the demo tenant pinned route name, not a moving catalog alias)
  - Single place to set `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_BASE_URL`, `REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID`
- Guardrails:
  - Refuses to run if pointed at a non-demo base URL unless `ALLOW_NON_DEMO=1` is explicitly set.
  - Redacts API keys from logs.

## Why native SDK vs OpenAI-compatible endpoint
We use the native Redwood SDK client here to avoid drift in parameter naming and to make it easier to highlight Redwood-only features (structured output helpers + tool call ergonomics). The CLI exposes an `--openai-compat` flag as a follow-up idea, but it is not implemented in this PR to keep scope tight.

## File/area summary
- `apps/sales-demo/`
  - `src/server.ts`: minimal web server + SSE streaming bridge
  - `src/scenarios/*.ts`: scenario scripts (single responsibility, deterministic)
  - `src/tools/*.ts`: tool definitions and stubs (order lookup, weather)
  - `src/structured/schema.ts`: JSON schema + runtime validator
  - `src/redwood/client.ts`: SDK client wrapper + retries/backoff
  - `src/goldens/*.jsonl`: expected outputs (line-delimited JSON events)
- `apps/sales-demo/README.md`: run instructions + talk-track mapping
- Root changes:
  - `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: add the app to workspace
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: run lint/typecheck/unit tests for the new app

## How to run (SE quick path)
1) `pnpm i`
2) `cd apps/sales-demo`
3) `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` (scoped demo key)
4) `export REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://api.demo.redwoodinference.com` (demo env)
5) `pnpm demo:run --scenario 01-core-chat-streaming`

## Determinism notes
- We set `temperature=0` and fixed `seed` where supported.
- Prompts are designed to be stable and avoid long-form free generation.
- Golden outputs assert on structure (event types + required fields + schema validity). We do NOT assert exact token-by-token text for streaming events to avoid flakiness.

## Tests
- Unit tests for:
  - Structured output validation
  - Tool call dispatch (ensures tool args match expected schema)
  - Retry/backoff behavior (fake timers)
- CI: `pnpm -C apps/sales-demo lint && pnpm -C apps/sales-demo test && pnpm -C apps/sales-demo typecheck`

## Screenshots / demo notes
No screenshots in this PR. The UI is intentionally minimal; primary demo path is CLI + optional browser view for exec-friendly viewing.

## Follow-ups
- Add a small "scenario index" page with one-click run + copy-to-clipboard outputs.
- Add optional OpenAI-compatible transport mode for customers who want drop-in testing.
- Wire this into the demo tenant reset to automatically run 1-2 scenarios and populate Console traces.

## Release / rollout
Examples repo only; no product release notes.

Refs: PM-197 (known-good scenarios), ENG-4821 (demo tenant automation; this app is a consumer).

review_conversation:
Monica Patel (SDK lead): Can we avoid asserting exact streamed text? We’ve seen minor deltas across runtime builds even at temp=0.
Renee Sullivan (author): Agreed. Updated goldens to validate event shape + final message JSON schema only; streaming asserts are limited to ordering + presence of assistant role events.

Markus Klein (Demo technical owner): Please add a hard guard so reps don’t accidentally run this against prod or a customer tenant.
Renee Sullivan: Added `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` allowlist check and requires `ALLOW_NON_DEMO=1` to bypass. Also redacts key in all logs.

Alex Martinez (DevEx): Can we include a small snippet in README that aligns exactly with the talk track steps? Also please keep env var names consistent with other internal docs.
Renee Sullivan: Updated README with a "Talk track mapping" section and standardized env vars to `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_BASE_URL`, `REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID`, `REDWOOD_DEMO_MODEL`, `REDWOOD_DEMO_MODEL_VERSION`.

Elliot Price (Docs & enablement): The scenario names are a bit long; SEs will be typing them live. Any alias support?
Renee Sullivan: Added `--scenario core`, `tools`, `json`, `retries` aliases in CLI.

Monica Patel: One more: structured output schema validation should fail fast and print the invalid path. Otherwise debugging mid-demo is painful.
Renee Sullivan: Added zod-style error formatting that prints the JSON pointer path and expected type; CLI exits non-zero and prints a "backup mode" hint.

Approvals:
- Monica Patel: Approved (after goldens change + error formatting)
- Markus Klein: Approved (after base URL guard)
- Alex Martinez: Approved
- Elliot Price: Approved
